chunks: [A part of the same sermon about the Holy Prophet] His place of stay is the best of all places,
and his origin the noblest of all origins in the mines of honour and the cradles of safety.
Hearts of virtuous persons have been inclined towards him and the reins of eyes have been turned towards him.
Through him Allah buried mutual rancour and put off the flames of revolt.
Through him He gave them affection like brothers and separated those who were together (through unbelief).
Through him He gave honour to the low and degraded honour (of unbelief).
His speaking is clear and his silence is (indicative) like tongue.
ai.seo_question: How does the sermon describe the spiritual and social impact of the Prophet's presence and character?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Radi presents this eulogy as a theological affirmation of the Prophet’s ontological perfection, framing his lineage and character as the ultimate source of divine grace (karāmah) and peace (salāmah). The text emphasizes his role as the unifier of the believers, transforming social discord into brotherhood, while his speech and silence serve as complementary modes of guidance. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the Prophet’s comprehensive authority, where his very being and actions establish the standard for spiritual and social order.
